notes.text:
Updated icu packages that fix a security issue are now available for Red
Hat Enterprise Linux 5.

This update has been rated as having moderate security impact by the Red
Hat Security Response Team.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The International Components for Unicode (ICU) library provides robust and
full-featured Unicode services.

A flaw was found in the way ICU processed certain, invalid byte sequences
during Unicode conversion. If an application used ICU to decode malformed,
multibyte character data, it may have been possible to bypass certain
content protection mechanisms, or display information in a manner
misleading to the user. (CVE-2009-0153)

All users of icu should upgrade to these updated packages, which contain
backported patches to resolve this issue.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

notes.text: International Components for Unicode (ICU) 4.0, 3.6, and other 3.x versions, as used in Apple Mac OS X 10.5 before 10.5.7, iPhone OS 1.0 through 2.2.1, iPhone OS for iPod touch 1.1 through 2.2.1, Fedora 9 and 10, and possibly other operating systems, does not properly handle invalid byte sequences during Unicode conversion, which might allow remote attackers to conduct cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: icu: XSS vulnerability due to improper invalid byte sequence handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary
